newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak VSZ still seeking merger with Czech Trinec.
newsitem.headline: Slovak VSZ still seeking merger with Czech Trinec.

text.p: Merger negotiations between Slovak steel maker VSZ a.s. and its Czech counterpart Trinecke Zelezarny a.s. are still ongoing, the Slovak economic daily Narodna Obroda reported on Friday.
The two firms signed a contract on Wednesday allowing VSZ to eventually buy up to 20 percent stake in Trinecke, which, in turn, could take 10 percent of VSZ.
The paper said the actual capital merger should take place some time in October, though its mechanism is still a subject of negotiation, possibly through a transfer of shares via stock exchanges.
"We are only in the stage of analysing and searching for an advantageous way to merge," Jan Smerek, VSZ President, was quoted as saying.
He added that a capital merger "does not have to mean" the creation of a holding company.
Smerek said the merger was a "top form of cooperation" and forms a solid basis for boths companies to further expand production.

"Such important capital participation...allow a very active intervention in all fields of a strategic management of the other side," Smerek said, not specifying further. "Not expanding means shrinking, and stagnating."

The agreement, signed at an engineering fair in the second Czech city of Brno, also called for both companies to open negotiations with Poland's Huta Katowice on integration of central European steel companies.
"Our mutual goal is to create out of the huge potential we have, a partner able to compete with the biggest world metal producers," Smerek said.
